A typed but malformed request fails rather than silently becoming an ordinary event. ## 7. Actual-value filtering **C07.** A filter is a Language definition tested against the actual event. It MUST NOT be merged into the event as a way to create missing event data. The selected exact algorithm is `Bridge.matches`: 1. Obtain the actual exact value and validate it as a value; obtain the filter as a definition. Resolve required exact evidence. 2. Walk actual and filter recipes together. For every authored or concrete inherited filter field, require the corresponding actual field and a present actual value. Typed declaration holes contributed only by a standard definition are not invented required business fields. 3. For filter list positions, require the corresponding actual positions. Extra actual positions or fields are allowed unless applicable Language constraints forbid them. 4. When the pattern names an explicit type, require that exact type in the actual value's type ancestry. This prevents unrelated registered notification types with structurally compatible fields from becoming indistinguishable. This is a Contracts filter guard, not a change to Language structural refinement. 5. With presence established, apply the selected Language refinement/validation operation to check fixed values, types and constraints. Return false for the defined compatibility, fixed-value, schema, list-shape and present-value mismatch categories. Propagate missing resources, invalid evidence and unsupported conditions as errors rather than false matches. 6. Never replace or alter the actual value. Pairwise visited-recipe tracking makes repeated/cyclic structure finite. There is no universal filter-depth ceiling. Demand-driven matching charges its prescribed logical work, retains repeated-pair cycle detection, and may be physically interrupted only as incomplete execution. Event fields inherited from the actual event's own valid type count as actual fields. Fields introduced only by the filter do not. A filter `{kind: paid, amount: {type: Integer, schema: {minimum: 100}}}` matches an actual paid event with amount 120, not one with amount 20 or no amount. A filter on a containing event must use its actual nested shape. `call` does not silently redirect ordinary filters to the operation request. For Embedded Node Channel only, its channel-level filter tests the inner application event. Its workflow-level filter and `$event` see the complete Embedded Event Delivery wrapper. This difference is explicit and does not apply to external events. ## 8. One selected operation call **C08.** Before external handler effects, perform precisely this recognition: ```text if originalEvent is a recognized Operation Request: call := originalEvent else if originalEvent's immediate operation field is a recognized Operation Request: call := that complete field value else: call := absent ``` The first branch has precedence. There is no recursive search, configurable selector, message extraction or second processing invocation. Unrelated ordinary events may still trigger ordinary workflows. Validate a recognized request's complete shape, nonempty channel and operation keys, optional Boolean precondition flag, and required exact-document reference when the flag is true. Its request arguments are not synthesized. During accepted-channel selection, freeze ordinary observer channels separately from operation recipients. An unaddressed request selects members whose accepted external channel key equals its channel; the named operation is checked only after selecting those candidates. A differently named observing channel does not make its member an operation target. For an explicitly addressed request, the installed verifier establishes the target lineage, independently of ordinary observation rights. On an actual recipient require the target channel to exist and be accepted. When that target channel is fresh, require the named Sequential Workflow Operation, its exact declared channel, and its optional argument definition to match the actual request value. All selected calls are validated before any event's business handler effects in this attempt. **C09.** `requireExactDocumentVersion: true` compares `document.blueId` with the exact target member BlueId from the **input graph**, before this attempt's initialization, another member's work or handler effects. Equality of resolved business projections is insufficient. No retargeting occurs. When the flag is false or absent, the optional document field imposes no exact-version restriction. Without a declared request definition, absent request arguments are permitted. Only the operation on its declared fresh target channel is eligible. Observing this event through another primitive or union channel does not invoke it again. A new observer union seeing an already consumed call does not repeat the target channel's operation, request validation or exact-version precondition. ## 9. External channel acceptance, lifetimes and checkpoints ### 7.1 Deterministic acceptance **C11.** Offer the complete external event to primitive external channels in every active member of the input graph. A standard External Channel accepts when its optional filter matches. An installed deterministic external-channel runtime returns a Boolean acceptance decision from its frozen header, complete original event, timestamp, previous checkpoint and explicitly declared peer access. It cannot replace the event. Compute each union's transitive primitive-leaf set, rejecting non-external members, missing names, duplicate direct members and composition cycles. A union accepts if at least one of its leaves accepted. Set semantics ensure that overlapping paths contribute one acceptance for that union. Empty composites and All External Channels over no primitives accept nothing. A document that accepts no primitive does not execute or validate a local named call. A document that accepts the event must have a compatible target for its recognized call when fresh work is selected. Thus broad bare channels on several members deliberately expose the same event to those members; intended discrimination belongs in channel acceptance filters, not a hidden documentPath parameter. ### 7.2 Freshness and no invented ordering protocol **C12.** This revision's built-in local checkpoint rule suppresses an exact repeat of the **last successfully consumed event** in a channel lifetime. If checkpoint event ID equals incoming original event ID, timestamps must also equal; equality produces no new consumption, and a changed timestamp produces `EVENT_TIMESTAMP_CONFLICT`. If the event ID differs, the input is fresh for this built-in rule. This is not an all-history deduplication service or a source-order protocol. Contracts does not reject a distinct event solely because its timestamp is lower. A host requiring ordered history or permanent occurrence uniqueness must establish it outside Contracts, or install a precisely bound deterministic channel runtime that verifies the relevant actual event evidence. Equal business payloads used as different external occurrences need distinct original external content; changing only the supplied timestamp does not give an identical checkpointed event a new identity. Primitive and union checkpoints are independent. Consuming a union does not advance a leaf that did not consume this event. Accepted input with no matching business handler still advances its checkpoint. Internal events do not. ### 7.3 Channel lifetime identity A primitive lifetime signature binds its exact runtime type and acceptance definition. Extension signatures also bind the complete extension specification and header fields. A union signature binds its exact type, sorted leaf names and the current leaf signatures. A changed acceptance or membership signature starts a new serial generation; removal retires the lifetime. Ordering-only edits do not create a fresh acceptance lifetime. A frozen seed is eligible only while the same member activation and channel generation remain live. Removal, replacement or changed acceptance cancels remaining old work. Checkpoints belonging to retired generations are reset during final settlement. This prevents an old checkpoint from being silently transferred to a different channel at the same key. ## 10. Deterministic completion machine **C13.** All implementations execute the same logical machine: ```text verify exact inputs, configuration and the input graph freeze primitive/union acceptance and validate selected calls if the root is already terminated: return TERMINATED establish input initialization using completed child results process dependency units before their containers run document-local turns drain only that document's local queue settle its eligible markers and checkpoints seal the completed result incorporate completed child results before their parent observes events finish required cyclic rounds and dynamic initialization finalize the exact graph and verify every affected containing context return one atomic APPLIED result ``` A dependency unit is initially a strongly connected component of the active managed graph. A singleton without a self-edge is an acyclic unit. Units run dependency-first. Internal graph membership and queues are private processor state; no public delivery wrapper is added. For a static DAG and one input phase, a member with work has one local turn: it first incorporates all required completed direct-child results, processes their queued events, then handles its frozen external seeds. Its output is not handed upward between channels, patches, steps or event handlers. Initialization is a separate no-external-input phase; its output is not replayed as external work. A member with neither new child state/events, initialization nor fresh seeds is carried unchanged. Every required header and acceptance fact is still verified; an optimization cannot skip ordinary workflows or another accepting channel merely because one operation name is known. ### 8.1 Fixed ordering Use the defined exact member keys, NFC token rules, decoded pointer rules and Unicode code-point comparisons. Condensation dependencies precede containers; among ready components choose the lexicographically smallest sorted member-key tuple. Within a cyclic round, visit members in key order. Physical completion order is never a tie-break. For each receiving turn, order source completions by source member key; within a source, order its completed batches by source turn serial. Within a batch, iterate event ordinal first, then the receiver's eligible occurrence paths and generations. Thus two occurrences of one child see `E1/path1, E1/path2, E2/path1, E2/path2`. Equal-content emissions remain distinct occurrences. Install all required incoming source states before invoking any receiving handler, validate the resulting receiving view, and append all initial incoming event occurrences in that order before draining. Events emitted by the receiver append to its queue tail. After that drain, execute its surviving external seeds in channel order, draining local events after each seed as in the defined. Incoming work can terminate the receiver or retire a seed before its direct external handling. Channels and handlers retain `(order, raw contract key, exact runtime type ID)` with zero default order. The stable bottom-up merge comparator in `LogicalWork.ordered` fixes comparison gas.
